---
name: add-byok-provider
description: Add or maintain a built-in BYOK media provider in the OpenMotion repository, including official API research, credentials, model discovery, generation adapters, editor configuration, provider references and verification. Use for contributor requests to integrate a supplier; ordinary media generation uses the openmotion-media Skill.
---

# Add a BYOK provider

Use this repository-local contributor Skill to implement a provider through the existing `openmotion_media_use` Tool and Model Gateway. Read the checkout's `AGENTS.md` and follow its current development/PR rules. Paths below are relative to the repository root. This Skill stays in `.agents/skills/`; product guidance ships from root `skills/`.

Start with [gateway behavior](../../../docs/model-gateway.md), then inspect the current callers and the closest existing adapter. Use Atlas for a shared image/video/audio prediction API, fal for returned queue URLs, WaveSpeed for authenticated discovery, and OpenDesign for a custom HTTPS gateway. Check current code instead of copying an entire provider or its assumptions.

## Establish the provider contract

Find and read the provider's official API/model documentation. Record source links and the date checked in its reference. Establish:

- Stable provider ID, display name, key-creation URL, API origin and authentication scheme.
- Whether model discovery is public or authenticated, response fields, pagination and model-specific schema links.
- Supported image/video/audio operations, exact model IDs, required fields and sample outputs. Separate speech from music/SFX and media files from transcription, text, training or 3D results.
- Submit and poll endpoints, remote task identity, intermediate/terminal statuses, output retrieval, cancellation and idempotency semantics.
- HTTP errors versus envelope/task codes, rate limits and uncertain outcomes. A 401 alone does not prove an incorrect key; consult the provider's actual semantics.

Implement only confirmed API behavior. Do not invent a model catalogue endpoint, account entitlement, unsupported modality, remote cancellation or refund. If documentation leaves a blocking ambiguity, explain the missing contract while continuing independent work.

## Extend the existing integration

Inspect these boundaries and update the ones the provider needs:

| Boundary | Current source | Required result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Provider registration | `shared/provider-registry.ts` | Register a dedicated provider's identity, setup links, API origin, endpoint editability, environment-key names and reference section here. Compatible presets are imported from `shared/provider-presets.json`. IDs and labels derive from this registry; do not add parallel lists in settings, HTTP or MCP. |
| Credentials and availability | `gateway/connections.ts`, `gateway/service.ts` | Reuse the shared configuration entry and existing file layouts, retaining saved-key priority, environment fallback, verification reset and save/remove semantics. A configured key enables the provider; it does not prove successful generation. |
| Model discovery | `gateway/catalog.ts`, `gateway/service.ts`, optionally `gateway/providers.ts` | Query the documented catalogue with the correct authentication. Normalize only supported media outputs; preserve pagination, caching and unavailable-catalogue warnings. Built-in fallback entries are optional examples, not a replacement for live discovery. |
| Generation | `gateway/providers.ts`, or a focused provider module | Implement `ProviderAdapter.generate` and register it in `providerAdapters`. Reuse persisted jobs, progress/remoteId, validation, downloads and project import. |
| Editor configuration | `gateway/settings.ts`, `studio/src/motion/ModelSettings.tsx` | Settings consumes registry metadata, including setup/reference links and endpoint editability. Reuse catalogue sync, capability filtering and the common default-model storage entry. Keep account authorization separate from provider API keys. Distinguish listed presets from implemented execution protocols. |
| Reference delivery | `shared/workflow.ts`, `server.ts`, `gateway/media-use.ts` | Register the provider document under media resources, plus the matching production alias kept for older clients, and include its HTTP reference route. Confirm inspect/reference/models accept and return the new ID. |
| User guidance | `skills/openmotion-media/references/providers/`, `references/jobs.md` in that media Skill, relevant `docs/` | Maintain one provider reference, listed in the media job procedure and available through the Tool. |

The public Tool already covers inspect/reference/models/generate/status/cancel. Reuse those actions; a supplier does not need its own MCP Tool or distributable Skill. Preserve the existing production routes and intentional UI visibility decisions. Tool and Skill lists come from their actual registries; do not introduce fixed quantity gates.

### Request and credential boundaries

- Inject keys only inside the service. Never read a contributor's real secret file, return a key to an Agent, add credentials to model parameters, or commit them. Use synthetic credentials in fixtures.
- Use the exact model schema. Some speech models expect `text`, others `prompt`; the existing mode controls that mapping. Cloud speech additionally nests options. Check the wire body, not just the Tool arguments.
- Keep fixed provider origins where possible. Any user-configurable origin must retain existing public HTTPS/DNS validation. Validate returned task IDs/queue URLs, and never forward authorization to an unrelated output or redirect host.
- Save the remote ID before polling and distinguish accepted, processing, failed and completed outputs. Do not automatically retry a paid POST, switch paid suppliers, or create a new task after a timeout. Check the original job/history first. Local cancellation/timeouts do not prove a remote stop.
- Reuse `apiJson`, media validation and project-owned imports. Recognize their limits: current non-2xx handling omits raw provider bodies/headers, and local errors can omit task detail. Do not promise full provider diagnostics or infer a definitive cause from generic local wording.

## Write the provider reference

Create `skills/openmotion-media/references/providers/<provider-id>.md` and register it as described above. Read one existing document, such as [Atlas](../../../skills/openmotion-media/references/providers/atlascloud.md), for the maintained shape; do not duplicate its supplier-specific facts.

Include key setup, authentication and model-list queries; `openmotion_assets_use` JSON templates for each supported modality; their exact HTTP endpoint/body mapping; polling/result retrieval; representative error codes with meaning, next action and retry boundaries; official source/model links and known integration limits. Distinguish Tool arguments from wire JSON, local job IDs from remote task IDs, and HTTP status from application/task codes. Mark unspecified behavior as unknown.

Keep real keys and internal/private source material out of the document. Put shell wire examples in this Skill's [wire examples](references/wire-examples.md), not in the product reference, using environment placeholders only. Direct Agents through the Tools so the service owns credentials. Templates do not execute paid requests by themselves. Do not add this contributor Skill to `packagedSkills`, workflow resources or host installation lists.

## Verify and hand over

Use deterministic fixtures to cover the new provider's real boundaries:

- Model discovery/authentication and normalization, including exclusion of unsupported output types.
- Public media Tool -> exact provider URL/auth/body -> original task polling -> validated project-owned file, for each implemented modality. Assert that an idempotent replay submits once.
- Rejected authentication/input and unsafe task/output destinations; errors or cancellation must not trigger another paid submission or expose a key.
- Configuration save/clear/remove, correct setup/reference links, catalogue refresh/error recovery, and default model selection.
- Reference delivery through Tool, MCP resources and HTTP, plus inclusion of the reference in distribution artifacts.

Adapt existing tests in `tests/byok.test.ts`, `studio/src/motion/ModelSettings.test.tsx`, `tests/workflow.test.ts`, `tests/npm-package.test.ts` and `tests/byok-browser.mjs`. Add assertions for observable behavior, not documentation wording. Ensure a new test file is included in the repository's explicit CI runner.

For runtime/Studio changes run `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck:studio`, `npm run build:studio` and affected deterministic/packaging checks under the pinned Node version. Use the shared browser-lock lane for real browser tests when available, or the exclusive isolated lane in `tests/byok-browser.mjs`; always use an isolated test project/data directory. Follow `AGENTS.md` when selecting narrower checks for documentation-only work.

Review `docs/product/architecture.md` and update it only if product behavior or boundaries changed. Report implemented modalities, references, actual checks, untested live-provider behavior and remaining limits. Run real paid generation only within the user's requested scope; fixture success is not account/billing or audiovisual acceptance. Commit/push/PR/merge/publication follow the current task authorization separately.

Accept automatic current-chat MCP activation independently; registration, a later connected chat and an independent probe do not prove it.

1. **Reuse setup.** Preserve its application, workspace, language and frozen three-of-four selection. If setup supplied no result, run the installed `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/install-onboarding.mjs` once with the connection's workspace and request language. Never reinstall or enqueue a user message.
2. **Check connection only as needed.** Reuse a successful same-chat workspace read from `hostHandoff.hostSessionVerified`; otherwise use a working native `openmotion_get_project` once. Registration or a separate process probe does not prove current-chat activation. If setup queued a refresh, finish this tool step and run the saved recovery command once; do not reload again. Read the contract's automatic-activation section only for a connection failure; do not scan sockets, change security or restart the host.

description: >-
  OpenMotion — Write a short product video script that plays like content rather than an ad: one angle, a concrete hook, the problem, on-screen proof, a payoff and one call to action, each beat mapped to a visual. Use before producing a product promo or creator-style ad.
---

# OpenMotion · Ad Script

Build the video as a native OpenMotion HTML/CSS/JS composition through the installed OpenMotion production Skill: create or open the project, author the composition, save with revision protection and preview. This library Skill adds creative direction only; it registers no MCP Tool or production route. Treat palette, font and timing values below as starting points; a supplied Brandkit or the user's brand wins. For missing images, voice or music, first discover providers and model IDs with `openmotion_media_use`, then generate with `openmotion_assets_use`; get the user's consent before any paid generation. Never invent quotes, numbers, specs or dates.

**Status:** recipe / draft. No executable template or rendered comparison yet.

**Use for:** product promos, app launches and creator-style ads that need a script and shot plan before anything is made.

## Look

| Element | Starting value |
| --- | --- |
| Script table | Time · Beat · Line · Visual, one row per beat; active beat marked in coral `#FF6B4A` |
| Preview | A 9:16 or 16:9 frame per beat beside the table, matching the target format |
| Captions | Bold sans, white, one coloured keyword per line |
| Tone | Spoken first person or a viewer-facing line; plain words, no slogans |

## Motion

- Hook in the first 1.5 s: a concrete outcome or a surprising, true line.
- One beat every 2–5 s: hook, problem, proof, payoff, call to action.
- Proof is shown on screen (a demo, a before/after, a real screen), not just said.
- The call to action fills the last 2–3 s and asks for one thing.

## Inputs

Required: the product page or notes with the claims that can be made, who the viewer is, length and aspect ratio. Optional: existing footage or screen recordings, the offer, brand voice. Offer 2–3 angles (pain, transformation, demo, objection) and write the chosen one in full.

## Avoid

Invented prices, numbers, guarantees, reviews or endorsements; feature lists in place of benefits; more than one call to action; visuals the user cannot actually make; naming competitors.

## Review

The first two seconds say why the viewer should care; every claim points to a source; the script reads aloud within the length; each beat has a visual and caption the user can produce.

skills.content:
---
name: openmotion-design-styles
description: >-
  OpenMotion — Apply a named design style to a short video: pick one of 21 style cards
  (Bauhaus, Swiss, Constructivism, Memphis, Pop Art, Risograph, Neo-Brutalism, Art Deco,
  Liquid Glass, Ink Wash, New Wave and more) or two layouts (Bento Grid, Masonry), each with a palette,
  open-licensed typefaces, five rules and signature motion, then plan, check and build the film so it
  reads as that style. Use when someone says "make this in Bauhaus style", "give my launch video a
  Swiss look", "which design style fits this?", "my video has no taste", or names any listed style.
  Produces a 10–20 second 1920x1080 HTML composition that shows the content through the style's rules,
  plus the checked plan file.
---

# OpenMotion · Design Styles

An OpenMotion Skill. The first beat shows the OpenMotion wordmark from `assets/brand/openmotion-logo.svg`
small in a corner (or styled into the scene); the last scene carries the credit "Made with OpenMotion".
A user's own logo and Brandkit colours are kept as supplied.

Say a style and a subject, get a film that teaches the eye that style while delivering the subject:
1. `plan.json`: the style, scenes, headlines and which style rule each scene demonstrates;
2. an editable OpenMotion/HyperFrames HTML composition with subset fonts;
3. a rendered MP4 when the user asks for one.

The film is only as good as the match between the subject and the style's own way of moving. Spend the
effort on step 2: decide how this style *itself* moves (a Bauhaus circle rolls, Swiss type snaps to the
grid, Neo-Brutalism presses onto its shadow) and build every scene from that, not from generic fades.

Build through the installed OpenMotion production Skill: create or open the project, author the
composition, save with revision protection and preview. This library Skill adds style direction,
a plan checker and a font helper; it registers no MCP Tool or production route. For missing images,
voice or music, first discover providers and model IDs with `openmotion_media_use`, then generate with
`openmotion_assets_use`; get the user's consent before any paid generation. Never invent quotes,
numbers, specs or dates.

## 1. Choose the style

```bash
node scripts/style.mjs list          # 23 cards: id, kind, render tier, one-line idea
node scripts/style.mjs show swiss    # palette, typefaces, five rules, motion, avoid, fits
```

- The user named a style: use it. They did not: offer two or three cards whose `fits` match the
  subject and say in one line why each fits; pick the first if they do not answer.
- `render` tells you the cost: `css` cards build with HTML/CSS/SVG and GSAP; `canvas` cards need a
  Canvas 2D layer (glyph grids, curves, ink, triangles); `webgl` cards (Diorama, Point Cloud, Liquid
  Chrome, Plush) can only be approximated in HTML. Tell the user before building a `webgl` card.
- A Brandkit or brand colours replace accent colours one for one; keep the style's ground, ink and
  proportions, or it stops being the style.

Done when: one card is chosen and you can state its idea line in your own words.

## 2. Plan the scenes and check the plan

Write `plan.json` (schema in [references/plan.md](references/plan.md)): 4–6 scenes, 10–20 seconds,
each with a short headline, the motion move it uses and the number of the style rule it shows.
At least two rules must be visible on screen; the last scene carries the OpenMotion credit.

```bash
node scripts/style.mjs check plan.json   # exits 1 on errors; fix and rerun until "ok"
```

Done when: the checker prints `ok` and every warning has been answered (fixed, or told to the user).

## 3. Fetch fonts

```bash
node scripts/style.mjs fonts plan.json <project-dir>
```

Downloads only the glyphs the plan uses for each card typeface (Google Fonts, open licences) into
`<project-dir>/assets/fonts/`, keeps each family's licence text and a `SOURCES.md` record beside them, and writes
`<project-dir>/fonts.css` with `@font-face` rules. Ship `SOURCES.md` and the licence texts with the project. Paste those
rules into the `<style>` of the file that uses them (HyperFrames lint requires the `@font-face` in that
file; a linked stylesheet fails `font_family_without_font_face`). Chinese text needs the card's `cjk` face, otherwise the render falls back to a default font.
It also scans every `.html` file already in the project (and `textContent` strings set from script),
so run it once more after building the composition and after any text change; otherwise labels that
are not in the plan render in a fallback font. Offline: use the nearest bundled HyperFrames font and say so.

## 4. Build

Follow [references/build.md](references/build.md): canvas, beat grid, how each card's rules turn into
layout and motion, and the brand beats. Use only palette colours (plus brand colours); put the rule
number and a short rule label on screen when the film is meant to teach the style.

Then `npx hyperframes check` and preview; render only after the review below passes.

## 5. Review

Walk [references/review.md](references/review.md) and report what you checked, frame by frame, from a
contact sheet and key frames. Do not self-certify that it "looks good"; name what the user still needs
to watch or hear.

The style list, colour values and rule topics were studied from the open design-style library
[guanmo-ai/design-style](https://github.com/guanmo-ai/design-style) by Guanmo (@guanmo_ai). That
